utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ramo Dzendusic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD S. LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He went out of my room, I told you that definitely, Room 16.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nail Hodzic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD S. LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was also in Room 13 or 15, but I cannot really vouch for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bico, the owner of the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD S. LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be the same thing. I don't know what room he was in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mustafa Kuloglija?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD S. LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came from the left wing, so either 13 or 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Engineer Granov?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD S. LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Left wing again, 13 or 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Atko Isanovic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD S. LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, that left wing. The majority were from that part because they had been brought earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Altoka?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD S. LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Esad Kiselica?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD S. LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he was in Room 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which room Kemal Dzelilovic was in?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD S. LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the room, but it is more than likely that it was the left wing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Seval Soro?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD S. LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which room exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But would you know whether he was in the left or the right wing?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD S. LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you, Witness. We do not have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Re-examination, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would like to clarify one matter. Re-examined by Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lojo, you have discussed the exchange or the release of the three Cengices, and just to clarify, who took them out from your room? Was it a regular guard, or was it someone else?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD S. LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a regular guard who came to get them out, the man who was on duty that day in the compound, I mean at our entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall who, who that was, which guard?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD S. LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, hardly, but he took us to the, to the door, that is, that metal gate, and then he turned them over to the next one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see to whom they were turned over? Could you see if it was another guard or someone else?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD S. LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another guard. As you open the metal gate, then you have another guard, except that from our room, 21 that is, I could not see the gate, the metal one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who actually ordered the guard who came to your room to take the Cengices out? Would you know that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD S. LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I could not know that. In principle, guards would either bring along a list, typed out if it was a larger group, or they would have a piece of paper with some names on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, no further questions, Your Honour. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, for giving evidence. You are now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honours, regarding the protective measures for the next witness, there is a matter that the Prosecution needs to discuss.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's FWS-35?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: It's 58, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Due to an oversight on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor, we did not request protective measures for this witness. However, during our proofing session, it became clear that he had originally asked for protective measures, and, therefore, we are making an oral motion now to ask for them. This was not through any change of mind on behalf of the witness but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just the sheer negligence of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What are the protective measures he seeks?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: He wishes to have a pseudonym, face distortion and voice distortion. I explained to him the concerns of the Trial Chamber regarding voice distortion and he explained to me that the place where he lives now, he is in very close quarters with other refugees, and in particular with Serb refugees, and because this proceeding is being followed very closely by the refugee community there, he is very concerned about being recognised by people with whom he is presently in contact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I see. Well, Mr. Bakrac, apart from your usual objection, have you got anything in particular about this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do not think there is any purpose in repeating, as you say, my usual objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I do have to add something. Since the OTP said it was their mistake, their error, the Defence understands that and we have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, then, we will make the orders sought for protective measures and the blinds can be brought in so the witness can be brought -- this is a voice distortion, too?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes. We have notified the audio-visual unit and they have the microphone set up. They just need a minute or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Right. Does this change of order mean that we are not going to hear FWS-35?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: No, he is here also. It wasn't a change of order; that has nothing to do with anything the court needs to be concerned with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I would also like to get a Prosecution exhibit number for the confidential name sheet that has been distributed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P424 and it will be under seal. After all of that, we can now have the witness. Thank you, usher. Have we any evidence in this case as to what happened to Pero Elez or am I only relying on something I heard in the previous case?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We had put in a series of newspaper articles that described his death.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Would you stand up, please, sir? And would you make the solemn declaration in that document that's handed to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: [Witness answered through interpreter].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sit down, please, sir. Move your chair up as close as you can to the table and speak directly into that microphone. Please do not answer any question until it has completely finished because if our microphones are left on, then you are not given the protection of voice distortion. Ms. Kuo?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want to confirm with the audiovisual booth that the voice distortion is in place. Thank you. Examined by Ms. Kuo:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me explain to you that the court has granted your request for protective measures, which means that you will have a pseudonym, there will be a facial distortion of your video image, and there is also voice distortion of your voice. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have before you Exhibit P424 which has FWS-58 indicated on it. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: I understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see -- underneath that, do you see your name?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Underneath your name, is that your birth date?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in 1992, what town or village did you live in?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: I lived in the village that I was born in, and that's the village of Crnetici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you can put the piece of paper away. It's no longer necessary for you to read it.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Put it away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With whom did you live?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: I lived with my wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you working at that time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you retired?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What ethnicity are you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village that you lived in, was it predominantly Muslim, Serb or mixed?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Mixed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the war started in Foca, on the 8th of April, 1992, could you hear it in your village?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you able to hear?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: We could hear from afar, and it is 11 and a half kilometres from town to my village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kinds of things could you hear in your village?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: We heard shooting from small arms, from mortars, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any residents leave your village?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Not then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they leave after that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they Muslim or Serb villagers?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Muslim, except for one family that had two little girls. They lived on the very outskirts of the village and they went somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why the Muslim residents of your village left?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Well, people know the conflict broke out in Foca itself. This was a prepared aggression. They started shooting a year before that, around all villages, all localities in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the Muslims specifically targeted in your village?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know in what way?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Let me just add something. Not in my village but throughout my municipality and throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina, the method was the same, the same method of attack and intimidation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to us why the Muslims felt intimidated and not the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Well, I'll tell you why. I'll try to speak slowly. While I worked -- actually I retired in 1991, and it was already then that Serbs started organising themselves and provoking conflicts within the authorities. They did not agree to any sharing of power or establishment of power which was characteristic of all municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in 1992, were there specific threats made to Muslims that caused them to leave your village and other villages?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear them or do you know what they were?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Well, simply at all crossroads, intersections in villages, in towns, everywhere, there were checkpoints and not a bird could fly by without being stopped or seen or caught.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave your village or did you stay?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Well, I'll try to explain this to you, the order. On the 8th of April, as far as I can remember, and I still can remember, in town itself, these clashes started. There was some group of, I don't know, 30 or 40 men, and they had had weapons. This was in the so-called area of Donje Polje. On the 8th of April, they started shelling Foca, the town itself. There was gunfire, mortar fire, and that's where they clashed. There was shooting. I was in my village so this is far away but you can still hear it, though it is muffled. They held Donje Polje and also the barracks of the KP Dom, or rather the building of the KP Dom. This was six or seven days, I don't know exactly for how long. Since there was such a lot of organisation and such a lot of supremacy on the part of the local Serbs, and then also there were paramilitaries from Serbia and also from Montenegro, they withdrew across the bridge which is near the KP Dom on the left bank of the Drina, and on the right bank of the Drina, they took buses to Gorazde. Then --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we focus, please, on the time after the war and the shooting had started in Foca. And you explained that certain villagers left. I'd like to know whether you also left your village.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: The chronology as to how all of this happened is coming in a minute. We were hiding like mice in houses, in forests, and this went on until the 27th of April. I remember that very well. Then, on that day, the Serbs proved that our village would be shelled. We thought that they were just trying to scare us and that they wouldn't do it. And in the early evening hours, say between 4.00 and 5.00 in the afternoon, they indeed started shelling and they allegedly told us to hide in basements. It's a mixed village so they did not hit any houses. They actually targeted the forests above the village. I did not measure time so it went on for an hour or two. I don't know, but it was in the early evening and we hid behind the house by a little stream. Night fell and I remember very well that my wife then came from Gorazde. Across the hill, there is this village of Sorlaci and we were near the road that goes by that stream, which actually wasn't up there. So we heard the shells flying over. You know, you can hear this whistle, like shell -- you can't hear a shell when it's falling but you can hear it when it's flying above your head. And also we saw them fall, and we saw and heard the explosion and the smoke. When all of this stopped -- I forgot to tell you something else. My wife came and this other woman also came, and we called out to them, and said that they should come down, and that's where we spent the night. And then later on, I don't know whether this was an hour or two, then this -- the Serb soldiers, some people call them the Chetniks -- well, they are some kind of soldiers one way or the other. And a neighbour of mine, (redacted), who used to come to my house even, he was in front of them, and they were going by, strictly in military order. We saw them approaching the house, and then one would get to a shelter and the other one would proceed and then this other one would reach the first one and that's how they went. And then they came to Zijad Cisija's house. His mother was old and she had to walk with a walking stick, and she couldn't stand straight. They searched the entire village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just a moment. Ms. Kuo, I know you've tried your best. I'm rather tempted to say that there is very little dispute, if any, that there were attacks upon the Muslim civilian population. There is an attempt to show that there was also attacks upon the Serb population with which we're not really concerned. May I suggest that you just lead him directly to the particular incident you want him to add to the extensive evidence we've already got on that, and that might save all of this detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will try to direct this witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- please, Witness, listen to the question and answer just Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the question, okay?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: I'm listening, I'm listening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see villages burning during this time, and if you did, could you tell us just the names of the villages?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: I did not see it. There is this one village that you cannot see, but you could see thick smoke. It's three kilometres away through the forest, across the hill, but you could see this thick smoke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of that village?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Gudelj was the name of the village, and next to it is Ribari, and also Karacic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those Muslim or Serb villages?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Gudelj is a mixed village, Serb and Muslim; Ribari is purely Muslim, and also Karacic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the houses in your village were all searched, or were only Muslim houses searched?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Only Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any Serb soldiers ever threaten you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: They were intimidating us. They were cursing at us when they were searching us. No, they were not searching us then. We were by the stream that day. But they did the next day, the next time. We'll come to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to leave without -- did you need permission to leave?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: We could try, because we were being told, we were being warned, that there was no place for us there, that we had to leave. But it was not possible to leave without a permission or without somebody's protection. From the municipality, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, from whom would you need to get permission to leave, what authority?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: We needed permission from the Crisis Staff in the municipality. That's where this was being settled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you yourself able at first to go to the Crisis Staff to get permission to leave?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: [No translation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you send someone on your behalf to go?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that person of Muslim or Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When that person returned, did he tell you, was he able to get permission for you to leave?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you need to go to the Crisis Staff yourself?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: No. Nobody made any offers to me, either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get your permit to leave? Did the Serb bring you the permit?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: This is the way it was: This neighbour of mine -- can I tell you in detail why we asked him to give it to us? Can I tell you about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Look, sir, I know that you are very anxious to tell us all of this, but we do have to limit ourselves to the matters which are in issue in this case. Just answer the questions that are being asked of you by the Prosecution. They are very well aware of what it is that they want you to say. I know you'd like to say more, but we really have to get on with this trial, and we do not have the opportunity to hear the whole history of this very unfortunate war. You proceed, Ms. Kuo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you yourself have to go to Foca to get permission to leave?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: It was not possible without an escort because anybody could kill you wherever you went. You were less protected than an animal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, you did go to Foca with somebody as an escort; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you go to Foca to get your exit permit? Is that the reason you were in Foca town?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: No. No, let me explain. My neighbour, that neighbour of mine, went on our behalf. He took all of our personal documents, and when he came back -- when they said that they would give it to us, he took all of our personal documents, our IDs, and took them to the staff, the Crisis Staff. And then he said, "You're going to get this and your documents stayed back there at the police station at SUP."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to the SUP in Foca to get your documents so you could leave?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were you in Foca on the 8th of July?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Haven't we understood each other? I never went. Did you understand what I said? That's why I had this intermediary who would bring this for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, at one point were you taken to Foca High School?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: I'll explain this to you. I have to explain this, the way it was. It's no good if I shorten things. I want to tell you the truth. This neighbour, when he brought this, he said, "You're going tomorrow." I can give you my neighbour's name, (redacted) (redacted). They took our things, and they put them in a car, a Lada car. And there were three disabled persons who could not walk, and they were also in the car, and the rest of us, we walked, with an escort. Without an escort, it was impossible to get to the municipality because we would not have -- we would not have arrived alive. Anybody could have killed you then. A ten-year-old child could have killed you and not be held responsible by anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: We took the village path, the village road to Josanica, that's four and a half kilometres. That is where the seat of the local commune is. It was an asphalt road, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived, did you receive your permit?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: In the meantime as we were walking, these disabled persons were driven to the school centre, and then this person returned to pick us up. I forgot: Some of the women walked. And I came in the car and two women, and also a man who was an alcoholic. We went to the SUP. And may I proceed now?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive your permit to leave when you reached the SUP?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: I told you, you didn't understand what I said. We were escorted by these two Serbs, and we arrived to the SUP. That is where we drove to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sir, did you pick up this permit at the SUP? That's the question. Now, that can be answered yes or no.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: I signed for all of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You proceed, Ms. Kuo.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: I have that permit in my pocket. I mean, it's there, it's been given there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you. With the assistance of the usher, I'd like to have item ID 119 shown to the witness. This should not be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the permit that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honours, we wish to have this entered into evidence as Prosecution Exhibit P119 with the translation as P119A with one correction. The date on the English translation is incorrect. If you look at the original, it's 7th of July, not 7th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objection, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. They will be Exhibits P119 and P119A, both of them will be under seal. Yes, Ms. Kuo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, it's no longer necessary for you to look at this exhibit. Witness, while you were at the SUP, did someone -- after you received your permit, what you've just looked at, were you allowed to leave Foca?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Precisely on that day we were supposed to leave; however, something came in our way - I don't know what it was - and then we were taken to the school in Aladza.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were taken to the school in Aladza, were there people from the village of Trosanj there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The group that was kept at the high school in Aladza, was it men, women, or children, or all of them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: This is the way it was: From Trosanj there was this one elderly man, around 70 years old. The rest were women and children, and also there were about seven or eight from Suljci, and also there was some persons I did not know, so perhaps 55 or 56 persons. And then after that they brought people in from hospitals and I don't know what all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, how many days did you personally stay at the high school?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: I stayed for seven days, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After seven days, were you taken someplace?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: I was taken by car. I knew that we would be going to Donje Polje. I said that to my wife. She was there. And I said, "Don't be sad. If they let you go, you should know where we are."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you told that you would be taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: This is the way it was: I think this was on the seventh day. There were 12 of us in the teacher's room, and the rest from Trosanj were in the classroom, and we were lying there. And on the seventh day a policeman came, a policeman, and there was this relative of mine who was an epileptic, and he went to another room, and then he came back, and then he said, "They're asking to see you." I walked in there and there was an officer sitting at a table just like this, and he offered me to sit down. And then he put this customary question to me, the usual question, "What's your name? Introduce yourself," naturally. And then the second question was, again, the usual one, "Where are your sons?" I said that I had no sons. "Who have you got?" (redacted) Perhaps I'm going on for a long time, but I have to tell you all the details. (redacted) (redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please do not give us those details, especially about your personal background. You've asked for protective measures, and if you give us details, you will be negating the purpose for which we have given you the protective measures. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Okay, fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I also know that you're very nervous. It will go much easier if you just listen to the question and answer it directly. Most of the questions I ask you will require just a very simple answer.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken from the high school? You don't need to tell us how, just where.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: The KP Dom, to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else was taken with you? How many people?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: I and two more men, Rahman, Adil and Sislija, Aziz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether your wife stayed at the high school, or was she taken somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: No. No, this is the way it was: After talking to that officer, he said to me, "The three of you will be going now, and the women and children will be going in the afternoon." I didn't know where. And they were taken to Partizan, to the hall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you were taken to KP Dom, what room were you placed in immediately?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: When I came to the KP Dom, in the office at the reception there was this duty officer and also these policemen and then this man who brought us in. There was the usual search, and then he issued the following order: "Take them to number three."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people were placed in Room 3 with you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: When we came there in front of the isolation cell, a man walked out, and Kulelija, Kulelija - I don't know what the name was exactly - put him in two, and the three of them put in number three. There were only three of us on this first day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The room that you were placed in, was it an isolation or solitary cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Yes. It was supposed to be for one person only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people were placed in it in addition to the three of you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: They would come from time to time. The next day there were four of us. This man was punished because he was looking out of the window. Whatever they did that was wrong, they were sent to isolation cells, and then the number went up, five, six, one night there were seven of us. And then when they would serve this sentence, so to speak, and they would keep them for as long as they wanted to, then they would take them back to the room, so then five of us stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many days were you personally kept in the solitary confinement cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Seven days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you taken? What room were you taken after those seven days?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: Room 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until what date were you kept in Room 11?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: They kept me in that room until I got out of the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us that date, please?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: I know the date, I haven't forgotten it. I can say that we were about to leave twice. First on the 30th of August we had set out, and then something got in our way. I don't know what happened. And then they moved us to the eating area number two, near where the -- near to where the vehicles got in, and we were there until nightfall -- before nightfall. Until five or six o'clock something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We only want to know the date that you finally left the KP Dom. Now, can you give us that date now, or we'll return to this in the morning?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58
utterances.text: I left on the 31st of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Good, thank you. We propose to adjourn now, but before we leave, would you please, sir, remain seated where you are until the blinds can be lowered and you can be taken out of the courtroom without being seen by the public. We'll adjourn now, we'll resume at 9.30 in the morning.
